title: Cyclone Safety
description: Cyclones are powerful rotating storm systems with strong winds and heavy rainfall. Proper preparation and response can protect lives and property during these severe weather events.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: A cyclone is a large-scale air mass that rotates around a strong center of low atmospheric pressure, characterized by strong winds and heavy rain. Cyclones can cause widespread damage through storm surges, flooding, and high winds. In India, cyclones commonly affect the eastern and western coasts. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issues cyclone warnings through color-coded alerts: Yellow (be updated), Orange (be prepared), and Red (take action).

sections.heading: Before a Cyclone
sections.content: Stay informed through radio, TV, and official weather updates. Secure your home by reinforcing doors, windows, and roofs. Trim trees and branches that could fall on your property. Clear drainage systems to prevent waterlogging. Stock emergency supplies including non-perishable food, drinking water, medications, flashlight, batteries, and first aid kit. Keep important documents in waterproof containers. Identify the nearest cyclone shelter and evacuation route. Charge your mobile phones and power banks fully. Keep your vehicle fueled and ready.

sections.heading: During a Cyclone
sections.content: Stay indoors and away from windows and doors. Do not venture outside even when the wind appears to calm, as the eye of the cyclone may pass and winds can return suddenly from the opposite direction. If advised to evacuate, do so immediately following official routes. Avoid using electrical appliances and stay away from water sources to prevent electrical shock. If you are outdoors, seek shelter in a sturdy building immediately. Do not take shelter in small sheds or under trees. If in a vehicle, stop in a safe location away from trees and power lines and stay inside.

sections.heading: After a Cyclone
sections.content: Do not leave your shelter until authorities declare it safe. Avoid driving or walking through floodwaters as they may be deeper or faster than they appear. Watch out for downed power lines and report them to authorities. Check your home for damage before re-entering. Use boiled or treated water for drinking until water supplies are declared safe. Help neighbors, especially elderly or disabled individuals, if possible. Follow official instructions for recovery and cleanup. Be prepared for possible flooding in the days following the cyclone.

sections.heading: Safety Precautions
sections.content: Never ignore evacuation orders from local authorities. Do not attempt to cross flooded roads or bridges on foot or in vehicles. Stay away from coastal areas during cyclone warnings as storm surges can be deadly. Avoid using candles or open flames during power outages. Keep emergency supplies easily accessible at all times. Do not spread rumors or unverified information during cyclone events. Follow official communication channels for accurate updates. Ensure that family members know how to contact each other during emergencies.
